mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases uncertainty and risk premia, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12mo moving average AND CPIAUCSL > 12mo moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12mo moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above their respective 6-month averages indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, which increases uncertainty and weighs on equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings behavior, which implies lower consumer spending and weaker corporate revenue prospects, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12mo moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
